draft.title: Youth perspectives on health
card: Different age groups can see health differently. Young people often describe health in terms of what matters in their daily lives.

Many young people link health to fitness, appearance, friendships and independence. Being able to play sport, look the way they want, keep friends and make their own choices can all shape how healthy they feel.
Adults often stress other things, such as preventing disease, managing stress, getting enough sleep or eating a balanced diet. Their view may look further ahead.
Neither view is wrong. The two can differ because age, experiences and priorities differ.
draft.remember: Young people often judge health by daily life, while adults may look more to long-term risks.

a.q: Which view of health is most likely to come from a young person?
opts: Being healthy means keeping my friends and my independence
Being healthy means having no disease at any stage of life
Being healthy means saving for a safe retirement
Being healthy means having regular checks for later illness
a.why: Young people often link health to friendships and independence, which matter in their daily lives. The other options focus on avoiding disease or planning far ahead, which is more often an adult emphasis.
a.clue: Think about what matters in a teenager's daily life.

b.q: Jas, 16, says he feels healthy because he plays footy with his mates and can choose his own weekend plans. His mother worries about his late nights and diet. What best explains their different views?
opts: They give weight to different priorities for their age
Jas is wrong and his mother is right about health
Jas has a physical view and his mother has a social one
Young people do not think that health matters at all
b.why: Jas links health to fitness, friends and independence, while his mother stresses sleep and diet, which look further ahead. Both views can be reasonable, so saying one is simply wrong is a tempting but incorrect answer.
b.clue: Neither person has to be wrong for the views to differ.

a.best: Being healthy means keeping my friends and my independence

b.best: They give weight to different priorities for their age

problems.detail: The right option is the only one written in the first person ('my friends and my independence'), so it sounds like a teenager speaking. A student could pick it from the voice alone, without knowing the idea.
